name: Ironpass Dock & Haul Full Kit
description: A harbor dockworker's full kit built for the wet, corrosive air of Meridian Harbor's lower loading decks. The outermost layer is a heavy-duty safety-orange weathershell jacket with sealed seams, acid-resistant coating, and a broad back panel printed with a white cargo handler designation number. The cuffs are wide enough to clear chrome forearm augments, with a secondary snap closure for a tighter seal in spray conditions. Beneath it sits a navy thermal henley with a reinforced neckline and flat-stitched seams to reduce pressure points under a harness rig. Cargo trousers in the same acid-resistant charcoal fabric as the jacket feature double-layered thigh panels, six external pockets with drain holes at the base, wide knee guards stitched in place with bright orange thread, and a reinforced crotch gusset for climbing and crouching. A name patch reading the wearer's dock assignment sits on the left chest of the jacket. Boots are heavy matte-black waterproof waders to mid-calf with steel toe caps, slip-resistant lug soles, and hook-and-bar lacing. A neoprene neck gaiter in navy rounds out the look, usually pulled down around the collar until the spray picks up.
functionality: Acid-resistant and waterproof outer shell, chrome-forearm-wide cuffs with secondary snap closure, drain-hole cargo pockets for wet environments, harness-compatible flat seams, reinforced knee and crotch panels for manual labor range of motion, steel-toe waterproof footwear, designation number printing for dock zone identification.
what_it_says: You move cargo for a living. You've been soaked through and dried out and soaked again so many times that your joints ache when the acid rain shifts direction. The designation number on your back is not a name but you've made peace with that. You know how to tie seventeen different load knots and you are not impressed by anyone who doesn't.
manufacturer: Ironpass WorkGear (street-adjacent industrial label, common in harbor districts)
story_hooks: A dockworker in this kit passes the players a cargo manifest folded inside their neoprene gaiter — the shipment listed doesn't match what was actually unloaded, and the designation number on their jacket places them at a berth that officially received nothing that night.

The acid-resistant coating on a particular jacket has been modified — someone has been using the outer shell fabric as a dead-drop surface, writing messages in a chemical ink that only appears under specific UV frequencies.
A dock worker is missing. All that's left at their assigned loading station is this kit, neatly folded, with the name patch cut out.
